why.description: Least privilege is justified per scope, or the scope does not ship.

never_requests.description: Positive commitment, fixture-checked: none of these appears in any authorization request.

oauth.description: The ACTUAL registered OAuth configuration, not a proposal. F11's callback framework and the connector must build exactly this route — a mismatch here is a silent install failure.

app_identifier.description: Provider-side app id, for traceability back to the registration.

token_exchange.description: How the code->token exchange authenticates. Stripe Apps use the DEVELOPER ACCOUNT'S API key for the installation mode, NOT a Shopify-style client secret — assuming otherwise is the most likely wiring mistake.

registration_status.description: Registration is NOT approval and NOT a working connector. Tracked separately on purpose.

clients.description: One entry per installation mode. Stripe issues a SEPARATE client_id for live, test and sandbox — using the wrong one for a connection's environment fails the install with a confusing error. Modelling it here makes that mistake unwritable. Single-client providers carry one entry with install_mode 'default'. client_id values are public (they appear in the authorize URL a user visits); they are not secrets.

install_mode.description: Provider's own name for the mode: live | test | sandbox | default.

environment.description: Which connection environment selects this client. null = any.

authorize_url_template.description: Verbatim authorize URL with {client_id} and {redirect_uri} placeholders, when the provider does not use a plain /oauth/authorize.

redirect_uri_operational.description: Whether the callback route is actually deployed and answering. Registered is NOT operational — every one of these is a build target until a connector proves otherwise.

granted_scopes.description: What the REGISTERED provider app actually carries today, verified against the provider — as distinct from `scopes`, which is what the connector needs and justifies. CI compares them in both directions: a required scope that is not granted is an install failure waiting to happen; a granted scope with no justification is over-permissioning and a §7 human-review escalation.

scope_deltas.description: Known, ACKNOWLEDGED differences between what the connector needs and what the registered provider app grants. CI fails on any delta not listed here — so a gap is tracked debt with an owner, not a permanently red build nobody reads.

closed_by.description: Task id that amends the provider app.

occurrence_key_template.description: The connector's default occurrence key derivation, for every event in `events` that does not declare its own. Placeholders are `{name}` tokens and the literal prefix is `{provider}:`. null = this connector cannot derive a stable occurrence key; its events are never correlated.

events.description: Optional (2.0.0-rc8). The event contract: each provider signal the connector projects, the event code it becomes, the projection allowlist, and the occurrence key derivation when it differs from correlation.occurrence_key_template. One signal means one code; several signals may share a code (a live and a historical order). CI checks each fixture case's expected envelope against it.

catalog_threshold_seconds.description: Past this, catalog availability becomes 'unknown' automatically.

lifecycle.description: All four are REQUIRED true by the launch gate (PROGRAM.md §8).

credential_kind.description: Enforced at issuance AND at use. An mcp_credential must never be usable as an ingestion or provider credential.

signal.description: The provider signal: a webhook topic, a virtual signal one topic carries (Shopify `checkouts/started`), or a plugin hook (WooCommerce). Unique within the manifest.

topics.description: The delivery topics that carry this signal, when they differ from the signal. A delivery is accepted once per selected signal it carries; a deselected sibling signal on the same topic is never accepted.

properties.description: The projection allowlist (contracts/01 invariant 7). Nothing else from the provider payload is stored. Empty = the event carries no properties.

occurrence_key_template.description: Overrides correlation.occurrence_key_template for this signal. Used when a repeated delivery must collapse to one occurrence (one checkout start per checkout, one delivery per fulfillment).

suggested.description: false = offered at setup but never pre-selected (Shopify order_placed duplicates order_paid for most stores).

historical.description: true = the signal only ever carries history imports. It never counts as live coverage and needs capabilities.history.

counts_as_activity.description: A commerce shopper action that may count as user activity (contracts/11, Commerce activity). Commerce connectors only; never a historical signal.

requires_scopes.description: Scopes the signal needs. CI fails when one is not requested in auth.scopes.
